title: Spark Caching & Persistence: Memory vs Speed

scenes.say: Ever wondered if caching your DataFrame in Spark really speeds things up, or just eats memory? Let's break it down.

scenes.label: Cache
scenes.sub: Stores DataFrame in memory to skip recomputation
scenes.say: Caching puts your DataFrame in memory, so Spark doesn't have to recalculate it every time you use it.
Cache is fast but uses memory. Persist lets you choose disk or memory, which is handy if you need to save RAM.

scenes.title: Cache vs Persist
scenes.say: Use cache for quick memory storage. Use persist with disk only if you want to save memory and don't mind slower access.

scenes.question: Should you cache every DataFrame?
scenes.right: No, only cache reused DataFrames and monitor memory to avoid spills.
scenes.say: Here's a classic interview trap: caching everything wastes memory. Only cache DataFrames you reuse, and keep an eye on your memory usage.
